traits.spine_sheath_colour.note: FNA vol. 4: 'sheaths uniformly whitish or pale yellow'; the flora gives no shade, so it was measured: the median of the non-green pixels inside the sunlit spine cover of seven iNaturalist photographs (imagekit batch inat-cacti-2026-10-19, photos 0, 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 10 in key order), the brighter three quarters of each, then the median of the photos: RGB 179, 161, 129, a pale straw (the photos ranged from 149, 140, 138 to 199, 177, 153).

traits.spine_cover.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), Cylindropuntia bigelovii var. bigelovii: 'Spines (8-)10-15 per areole, at most areoles, interlaced with spines of adjacent areoles, usually uniformly, diffusely spreading and nearly completely obscuring stem, pale yellow to yellow to tan, aging brown; abaxial spines spreading to deflexed, subterete to flattened, the longest (10-)15-25 mm; adaxial spines erect or spreading, terete, the longest (10-)20-28 mm; sheaths uniformly whitish or pale yellow, not obviously baggy.' A cholla's spines are not told into radials and centrals, so all of them are the radial set.

traits.note: Britton and Rose's The Cactaceae (vol. 1, 1919, p. 58), as Opuntia bigelovii: joints 5 to 15 cm long, very turgid, their tubercles about as long as broad; spines numerous and pale yellow, with papery sheaths, their count and length not given.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a trunk of joints 1 to 1.5 m tall with short branches of easily detached joints crowded at its top; lower branches fall away, so the trunk below is bare and dark. Joints 5 to 15 cm long and 3 to 6 cm thick. Pale green to yellow flowers at the joint tips in spring. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge: about a metre within 15 years. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: joints hidden under dense, barbed, straw-yellow spines in papery sheaths that shine silver in back light, darkening to near black on the old trunk. Its flower, bud and fruit are drawn from its characters by the rules at Cactaceae and the flowering plants: tepals on a spiral, as many and as broad as the family's rules give, on a floral cup above the inferior ovary, its stamens, style and stigma lobes, and its fruit from its stated colour, size and surface. Until 2026-10-18 its flower and fruit looks were partly set by hand (round tepal tips, a centre and an accent colour by eye), and a look set by hand keeps the rule that gives it the year its months state from running, so it flowered and fruited all year.

appearance.bodies.stem.spines.glochid.note: Britton and Rose's The Cactaceae (vol. 1, 1919, pp. 42 and 57 to 67): the areoles bear glochids above the spines, here not described for the species; the genus's are usually numerous, so drawn pale yellow like its spines. Their count, length and angle are set by eye like a prickly pear's, smaller, as no flora measures them.
